clinic should be called PROBLEM. Every time I want to make an appointment with a GP, I have to wait a month and go to the emergency department. Unfortunately, I couldn't wait a month. I needed antibiotics because this was my second serious cold, and they had a problem with it, and after an argument, I got them. It all comes down to arguing with people about getting decent treatment. Anything I don't ask for is a PROBLEM. I have all my medical records from my home country and I know what to do in a given situation, step by step. They tell me to get tested before seeing a doctor. Before I do, I have to wait another month in the NHS queue for an appointment. I want an appointment with a specialist who will help me, not get tests, because that's their procedure, and then wait in limbo for a referral, which takes another month if I want to see a specialist. Even when I call them and explain my condition, they can't help me or even give me a few minutes to talk to a doctor.
I don’t have a UK number. Telephone medical advice cannot be provided to overseas numbers, which creates problems, including for my husband who is working and I am unable to answer his phone. I am very sorry to hear how frustrated and unsupported you have felt when trying to access care. This is not the standard we aim to provide, and we appreciate the opportunity to respond to your concerns.

You raised an important issue regarding telephone access. Unfortunately, due to clinical indemnity and NHS regulations, we cannot provide consultations or medical advice to patients using non‑UK or overseas telephone numbers. This is because we must be certain that patients are physically within the UK when receiving medical advice, and we are legally indemnified only to treat patients located here.

We understand how challenging it is when appointments are fully booked, especially when you are unwell. Demand for GP appointments has been extremely high, and at times this leads to longer waits than we would like. If you’d like to get in touch with me directly by phone on 01480 483100 or email at acorn.enquiries@nhs.net we can investigate and support you further.

Yours sincerely
Victoria Pilkington
Practice
